name: Ashwort & Bone — Tier 3 Neighborhood Canteen Chain
creator: Founded by Mirela Johansson-Achebe and Prosper Nwosu-Vance, 2197
description: Ashwort & Bone is a 23-location neighborhood canteen chain operating primarily in Tier 2-3 zones of Meridian 88, founded in 2197 by culinary school graduates Mirela Johansson-Achebe and Prosper Nwosu-Vance on the principle of 'serious food at honest prices.' The menu draws deliberately from no single culinary tradition, rotating seasonally across West African stew bases, fermented Scandinavian fish preparations, Sichuan-inflected synth-protein braises, Persian rice formats, and Japanese pickling techniques, all executed with the same Compound Umami synth-protein base but with genuine care for preparation and seasoning. A full meal runs Φ8-16; the chain employs approximately 340 people across its locations and has a policy of hiring 40% of staff from Tier 1 addresses.
cultural_impact: Ashwort & Bone is frequently cited as the model for what accountable mid-tier food service can look like — profitable, community-embedded, and genuinely multicultural in its menu without treating any tradition as a novelty. Its hiring policy has been copied by several competitors, though not always with the same integrity of implementation.
controversy: In 2222, rumors circulated that a Tier 4 hospitality corponation had approached the founders with an acquisition offer; Johansson-Achebe and Nwosu-Vance issued a joint statement saying they had received the offer and refused it, but declining to name the company. Food industry observers noted that two Ashwort & Bone locations had quietly closed in the preceding six months.
story_hooks: One of the two recently closed Ashwort & Bone locations was in a neighborhood that has since seen rapid Tier 3-to-4 gentrification; a former employee believes the closure was not financial but strategic, and that the founders were pressured.

A longtime Ashwort & Bone line cook has been quietly developing a menu item that incorporates a fermentation technique from the Ferment Underground's supply chain — and it's become the most-ordered dish at his location without appearing on the official menu.

The 40% Tier 1 hiring policy has produced an unexpected situation: three current Ashwort & Bone employees have been identified by a gray-market runner network as persons of interest, and the chain's management must decide how to handle an inquiry from Axiom enforcement.
